News.title: Shock moment school bus is nearly wiped out by a TRAIN as kids scream in terror after reckless driver ignored warnings
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a school bus carrying almost 30 screaming students is nearly wiped out by a train.

Yvonne Hampton, 67, is accused of recklessly driving across the live tracks and leaving the rear end of her bus just inches away from being hit.





Hampton allegedly said as she approached the train line she was “not gonna stop for no train”.

The Floridian driver disobeyed railroad warning systems as she jolted across the tracks despite having 29 students and another adult on board.

Footage shows the yellow school bus trying to cut onto a busy main road as several cars drive past.



An impatient Hampton edges forward just as a train comes crashing past.

Sumter County School District Superintendent Logan Brown said that if the bus had been just six inches further back then it would likely have been an “extremely catastrophic situation”.

Scary video taken from one of the students sitting at the back of the bus shows just how close the train came to hitting them.

Several children can be seen rushing to the front of the bus as the train rushes on past while other pupils scream.



Terrified witness Christina Armstrong said she could see the panic on the children’s faces during the near miss.

She recalled: “The bus had stopped before the tracks, and then it started to go.

“A car had changed into the other lane, by the looks of it. I saw the bus pull forward, but not enough,” she said.

“I wanted to cry. I immediately started to pray afterward because it was a lot.”

Superintendent Brown praised the train conductor for sounding the horn to make Hampton pull forward.



He hailed them as “a hero”.

No one was injured on the bus or on the train.

Hampton has since been charged with 29 counts of felony child neglect and failing to stop at a railroad crossing.

She has also been fired from her job as a school bus driver in Bushnell, about 50 miles northwest of Orlando – a position she held for over a decade.

In response to the close call, the district has now changed all its bus routes so they divert around the train tracks rather than across them.

They are also reviewing their driver-hiring process.

News.title: Weather warnings issued across EVERY Canary Island during school hols as Atlantic storm brings 16ft swells & 45mph gusts
News.content:
DRAMATIC weather warning are continuing to hit a British holiday hotspot after authorities issued fresh alerts for towering waves and powerful winds.

The terrifying warnings have now been expanded to cover all seven Canary Islands as an Atlantic storm system pushes in from the north.





The raging weather threatens to whip up huge seas and gusts of up to 45mph in the coming days.

Spain’s State Meteorological Agency AEMET has activated yellow weather warnings across the region.

Forecasters warn conditions could quickly worsen along exposed coastline.

The alerts come just as thousands of British families prepare to jet out to the popular holiday hotspot for Easter half-term breaks.

Tourist favourites Tenerife, Gran Canaria, Lanzarote and Fuerteventura are all expected to see dangerous sea conditions, with waves forecast to reach between four and five metres.

The rough seas are expected to begin hitting the islands from Wednesday, particularly along northern and exposed coastal areas.

At the same time, powerful winds will sweep across the archipelago from Thursday, with gusts of up to 45mph predicted in mountainous areas and along exposed coastlines.



Authorities are warning residents and visitors to take extra care near beaches, harbours and cliffside viewpoints as conditions deteriorate.

The storm will affect each island slightly differently, but no part of the archipelago will escape the warnings.

Tenerife and Gran Canaria are expected to see strong waves battering most coastlines on Wednesday, before gusty winds slam northern regions and mountain slopes on Thursday.

On Lanzarote and Fuerteventura, rough seas will arrive on Wednesday, followed by island-wide strong winds the next day.

Meanwhile the smaller islands – La Palma, La Gomera and El Hierro – could feel the impact even sooner, with rough seas beginning from Tuesday evening in some coastal areas before returning again later in the week.



The Government of the Canary Islands has also issued a “pre-alert” for coastal phenomena, which came into force at 9pm on April 7.

Officials said the decision was taken using data from AEMET and other monitoring systems, under the region’s emergency weather response plan.

Authorities warned of north-west swells reaching three to four metres across the islands, alongside strong winds between La Gomera and Tenerife.

The swell is expected to peak with long wave periods before gradually easing during Wednesday morning, although conditions may still change as the storm system develops.

The unsettled weather is being driven by a low-pressure system moving through the Atlantic just north of the islands, dragging unstable conditions across the region.



Meteorologists say alerts are typically issued up to 48 hours in advance, meaning the warnings could still be extended or upgraded if the storm intensifies.

The system is also stirring up wild weather across mainland Spain, where forecasters are warning of intense thunderstorms, hail and heavy rain in parts of the country.



In regions including Castilla y León, Castilla-La Mancha, Extremadura and Galicia, yellow warnings are in place for storms and heavy rainfall.

Powerful gusts could exceed 45mph in some mountainous areas, while Saharan dust drifting across the atmosphere could mix with rainfall to create “mud rain”, a phenomenon that coats cars, buildings and roads in dirty residue.

Temperatures in the region are also expected to drop sharply in western Spain as the unstable weather pattern takes hold.

The latest warnings will ring alarm bells for many tourists after recent storms already caused major disruption in the Canary Islands.

Last month Storm Therese unleashed devastating flooding and landslides, leaving more than 3,000 people stranded or displaced in Gran Canaria alone.



Entire communities were cut off after relentless rainfall washed away roads and caused ravines to burst their banks.

Evacuees were forced to shelter in a secondary school while emergency crews battled the extreme conditions.

Popular tourist areas including San Bartolomé de Tirajana, Santa Lucía, Mogán and Telde were among the worst hit.

Mountain access routes became dangerously unstable, while coastal homes in Pozo Izquierdo were battered by fierce winds and sea spray.

In neighbouring Tenerife, winds reaching 73mph knocked out electricity and street lighting, leaving dozens without power.



Authorities are urging visitors to stay alert to weather updates and take care along exposed coastlines, particularly as winds and waves intensify later this week.

Just last week another popular tourist destination was plunged into chaos when a choking dust of Saharan dust engulfed the Greek island of Crete.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Storm Erminio also unleashed deadly flooding, torrential rain and snow across Greece – taking the life of a man in Athens.

The popular tourist destination was cloaked in an eerie red-orange haze as thick African dust swept across the island, turning skies apocalyptic and forcing planes to divert.

News.title: Fury as Travellers ‘bulldoze’ onto beauty spot with diggers & dump tonnes of tarmac before ‘making crowbar threats’
News.content:
LAND GRAB Fury as Travellers ‘bulldoze’ onto beauty spot with diggers & dump tonnes of tarmac before ‘making crowbar threats’

A HUGE traveller convoy has descended on a quiet village, with locals claiming they have been threatened with “metal crowbars”.

Dozens of caravans, diggers and bulldozers rolled onto a green belt field in Flamstead, Hertfordshire, over the Easter weekend.





Furious residents claimed the travellers arrived on the site telling them “say hello to your new neighbours“.

They say the group forced their way onto the green belt land before starting work laying concrete.

A 70-year-old pensioner living nearby said: “It’s like the Wild West. They are destroying the community.

Diggers and bulldozers moved onto the field off Friendless Lane on Thursday, with caravans following in the early hours of Sunday morning.

Villagers told The Sun they believe the land was deliberately targeted over the bank holiday weekend to avoid council detection.

They claim that this is the first time the site has been occupied by travellers, and at least 3,000 tonnes of rubble has already been dumped.

Exclusive aerial images reveal the extent of the damage, with the site, located in the Chilterns Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, torn apart.

The enraged pensioner added: “This is an area of outstanding natural beauty. The whole village normally wakes up to peace, but no longer.



“There have been a few violent outbursts when we tried to stop them getting in. We have had metal crowbars flung at us.

“They know what they’re doing – it’s like a military operation.”

One resident alleged a traveller tried to force entry after locals attempted to block access with a barricade.

Hertfordshire Police confirmed a cop car was damaged during the incident.

One exasperated resident said: “The council put a notice on the field which legally means work should stop, but no one is enforcing it.”



The pensioner warned the encampment could be permanent, saying: “These are big static caravans, they’re not workers’ huts. They are here to stay.

“They won’t stop intimidating us. One went up to my wife and said: ‘We have more money than you.

“Another said: ‘Say hello to your new neighbours. F*** you.’ We won’t put up with it.”

A spokesperson for Hertfordshire Police said: “While the civil matter is being led by Dacorum Borough Council we are continuing to monitor the situation and police patrols are being conducted in the area to prevent a breach of the peace and deal with any criminal matters.

A number of allegations have been made by several parties involved, including criminal damage and threatening behaviour.



“These matters are being assessed and investigated, and we will look to make arrests wherever necessary.

“If you believe a crime has been committed, please report it. In an emergency, always dial 999.

“In these circumstances, police have no enforcement powers to prevent access to the land or building work taking place.”

Dacorum Borough Council confirmed it has begun civil court action, securing an emergency injunction and is taking steps to halt the unauthorised works.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Council leader Sally Symington said: “These works are unauthorised and are a serious breach of the planning process.



“I share residents’ anger and devastation that a section of the community has ridden roughshod over the council’s planning processes.”

News.title: Ex-BBC producer found with 6,000 child abuse images and searched for ‘jailbait’ online, court hears
News.content:
'PAEDO' TRIAL Ex-BBC producer found with 6,000 child abuse images and searched for ‘jailbait’ online, court hears

A FORMER BBC producer was allegedly found with 6,000 images of child abuse and searched for “jailbait” online, a court has heard.

Dylan Dawes, who was a producer for BBC Wales, was arrested at his home in Cardiff in February 2022 where officers seized four of his devices.





The 50-year-old appeared at Cardiff Crown Court on Tuesday after images were found on a hard drive, a laptop and two iPads, reports the BBC.

Following his arrest, he told officers he had “no knowledge” of the images which the court heard were downloaded “during a period of time of about 16 years”.

It was also revealed that the search term “jailbait” was discovered on Dawes’ laptop.

According to the prosecutor, Harry Baker, Dawes began working at the BBC in 2001 and had been “downloading child pornography” between 2006 and 2022.



Following Dawes’ initial arrest at his home, he was escorted to Cardiff Bay police station by officers to be interviewed.

There he denied possessing or making indecent images of children and said he was “not aware” any were on his devices.

However, 483 images were found upon later examination, seven of which were Category A.

A Category A image ranks as the most severe type of child sexual abuse material under law.



Later, nearly 5,800 further images, including 185 Category A images, were recovered as having been contained on the devices at a previous point in time.

When invited to a second police interview in December 2022, Dawes said in a prepared statement that he had “no knowledge of any indecent images that were found on my devices”.

“I have never knowingly used, accessed or downloaded or sought indecent images of children,” he continued.

“I have no sexual attraction to children.”

Dawes admitting to downloading “regular pornography” and said his devices had been previously left “for extended periods in open plan offices”.



After delivering his statement, the 50-year-old declined to answer further questions from the police.

The court also heard that the search term “jail bait” was found on Dawes’ laptop with a file path linked to a folder called “Dylan”, according to WalesOnline.

He was asked by the prosecution if he could identify the person who had been using the devices to download the images so “they could be investigated”.

“He denied being responsible for the making of those images,” they said.

Dawes is accused of six counts of possessing or making indecent images of children which he has denied.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

When The Sun approached the BBC, the broadcaster said they could not comment on a legal case and Dawes was no longer a member of staff.

The trial continues at Cardiff Crown Court.

News.title: Landfill leaves town STINKING with vile ‘rotten egg’ stench that ‘makes residents vomit & suffer headaches’
News.content:
FURIOUS residents have staged a protest outside a stinking landfill as they say fumes from the site are making people feel sick.

Around 100 locals gathered and marched to the Jameson Road landfill site in Fleetwood, Lancashire, waving placards and blocking the entrance.





They have demanded action over the foul stench and called on Sir Keir Starmer to come and smell the conditions for himself.

Gasmask-clad demonstrators were seen stopping lorries from entering while shouting “Stop the smell” and “We want our voices to be heard”.

The landfill operator, Transwaste Recycling & Aggregates, says it is waiting for permission to seal up the site from the Environment Agency (EA).

And the EA pointed to several potential reasons behind the odour, including weather and “the natural acceleration of waste breakdown”.

Campaigner Allison Rowe said people in the town are “fed up” with the daily stink.

She said: “If I drive out of town and come back, I’ll vomit from it. We’re not going away.

“We are firm in our attempts to get that place closed, nothing else will do.”



Residents say the smell – often compared to rotten eggs or chemicals – has plagued the town for two years.

They have blamed it for nosebleeds, headaches and breathing problems.

Local MP Lorraine Beavers also joined the protest, saying families have “a right to breathe clean air”.

Some 20,000 complaints have been made to the EA about the landfill, with Transwaste having already been served an enforcement notice.

This required it to “ensure that areas of the landfill are adequately covered to reduce the risk of odour”.



Protest group Action Against Jameson Road Landfill was set up by resident Jess Brown.

The 35-year-old accused Transwaste of failing to manage the amount of gas that’s being emitted from the site.

Jess said: “You cannot escape the smell. It is literally as if you are being gassed.



“You cannot open the windows or go out because the smell is so terrible. Walking children to school is a nightmare.

“What is it doing to our health? No-one is looking at this properly to see what damage is really being done to people.”

A coroner undertaker went as far as saying the stench was worse that “houses where bodies have been undiscovered for months”.

Wyre council owns the site and receives £200,000 a year in rent from Transwaste.

The current lease runs until the end of 2027, but residents say they cannot wait that long.



Transwaste owners, Mercury Group, said it submitted a proposal for “permanent capping” in December and has been awaiting approval.

Capping is the process of sealing a filled or inactive landfill with a multi-layered cover.

It prevents rainwater from causing hazardous runoff and controls gas emissions and odours.

The waste firm said: “We have been in discussions with the EA this week and we are hopeful that given consent, we will be able to start permanent capping on Monday.

“The independent EA air quality monitoring indicates that air quality in the area is well within Word Health Organisation safety limits.”



The landfill was closed in 2017 but reopened in 2023.

The EA says reopening long‑inactive landfills can release gases including hydrogen sulphide.

This then produces a “rotten egg” odour, although the EA claims there are no health issues connected to the site.

A spokesman for the EA said: “There are several potential reasons behind the recent rise in odour.

“These may include the current weather conditions, the effects of the interim capping works, the natural acceleration of waste breakdown, or issues with how systems and processes are being managed on site.



“At this stage, there may be a combination of factors contributing to the problem, and we are continuing to assess them carefully.”

“The community should not have to tolerate odours that affect their environment.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We have pushed the operator to cover areas of the site where waste has recently been deposited to reduce odour and are pressing them to install permanent capping as soon as possible to prevent future emissions.

“Environment Agency officers are on the ground actively monitoring the situation, and if we don’t see improvements, we will not hesitate to take further enforcement action.”

News.title: ‘Disgusting’ chef kept fish in BATH next to toilet before selling it in ready meals to UK supermarkets
News.content:
FISHY BUSINESS ‘Disgusting’ chef kept fish in BATH next to toilet before selling it in ready meals to UK supermarkets

A “DISGUSTING” chef kept fish in a bath next to his toilet before selling it in ready meals to UK supermarkets.

Stephen Akuoko had been operating in Watford, Hertfordshire, under the name Tribal Foods for more than three years.





The 62-year-old flogged ready meals to supermarkets and corner shops in the area with inappropriately long use-by dates.

There was also a lack of ingredients listed on the products, which were described as “unfit for human consumption”.

Akuoko’s business was pursued by the council’s environmental health team but he proved elusive until a fire broke out at his flat in October 2024.

Firefighters discovered huge quantities of fish in the bath and on the floor of the bathroom next to the toilet.

Akuoko has now been handed a two year prison sentence suspended for two years after he pleaded guilty to two food safety offences.

He was also banned from operating any food business for five years by a judge at St Albans Crown Court.

Michael Coley, prosecuting, said the environmental health team began investigating Tribal Foods after finding its ready meals in local shops.



But the court heard the business was difficult to track down and when officers finally managed to speak to Akuoko on the phone, he became aggressive.

When food safety officers attended the flat after the fire, Akuoko claimed all the fish in the property was for him and his family.

He also assured officers they would not see Tribal Foods products in Watford again, but just weeks later, they found his unlabelled products in a local shop.

CCTV also showed him making three deliveries to one shop in a matter of weeks.

Mr Coley said: “This was an intentional breach and a flagrant disregard for the law.”



In mitigation, Aleister Adamson said Akuoko set up Tribal Foods after a period of homelessness.

He initially operated the business from a rented kitchen space before cooking from home, it was said.

Sentencing, Judge Francis Sheridan said: “Your little business got bigger than you could handle and you resorted to frankly disgusting techniques – fish on the floor of the bathroom, fish in the bathtub, and then you cooked them up and sold them.

“You must realise that food poisoning can have very serious consequences, even death, and if that had happened you would be facing manslaughter charges.”

Justine Hoy, Associate Director Housing and Wellbeing for Watford Borough Council, said: “Food safety laws exist to protect the public.



“In this case, there was a clear and sustained failure to comply with legal requirements, despite formal enforcement action being taken.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We will not hesitate to take action where businesses or individuals put public health at risk.

“This successful prosecution demonstrates our commitment to maintaining high food safety standards across Watford.”

News.title: Creepy moment school board member tells young student ‘God, you’re hot’ as he puts arm around her at meeting
News.content:
A SCHOOL board member sparked outrage after he creepily told a teenage student she was “hot” – while putting his arm around her during a public meeting.

Keith Ervin sidled up beside the high school senior moments after she addressed the panel, startling the packed room with the bizarre remark.





The disturbing moment unfolded during a Washington County school board meeting in Tennessee.

The girl had been speaking about potential school restructuring and the curriculum when Ervin approached her, triggering awkward laughter from the room as the meeting was livestreamed.

Ervin unnervingly put his arm around the girl and said: “God you’re hot, you know that?

“Where do you go to school at?” he asked in front of everyone.

READ MORE IN WORLD NEWS HUMAN TROPHIES Brit tourists 'paid extra to kill pregnant women & kids on human safaris'

When the student politely replied that she attends David Crockett High School, the board member simply grinned and said, “All right.”

Despite the stunned atmosphere, no one immediately challenged Ervin over the remark and the meeting continued as normal.

But the alarming clip quickly spread online – sparking fury and calls for him to be removed from office.



More than 3,400 people have since signed a petition demanding Ervin be ousted, along with Superintendent Jerry Boyd, who critics claim laughed during the incident.

“This is not the first time Keith Ervin has been in trouble for inappropriate conduct,” the petition alleged.

“Despite previous incidents, he maintained his position, raising questions about the accountability and integrity of those in power within our education system.

“Allowing such behavior to continue sets a poor example for our children and undermines the moral and ethical standards expected of educators and officials entrusted with our children’s education and welfare.”

Brad Arnett, who launched the petition, blasted Boyd for allegedly laughing at “this utterly disrespectful remark”.



He also accused officials of protecting each other through a “good ole boy system.”

“As a father of both a boy and a girl, I was appalled by the video, as anyone who is a decent human being should be,” he told WSMV.

Education board chair Annette Buchanan later said the remark “objectified and diminished” the student, who was a high school senior.

Parents were also stunned that none of the other board members immediately stepped in to defend the teenager.

“My initial thought on it was that the people were laughing afterward; no one bothered to defend her,” Melanie Bell told WJHL.



“They all seemed a little like, ‘Oh, this is nerve-racking.’ But they didn’t say anything.

“He’s an elected official, so he should be definitely minding his p’s and q’s, especially on camera, because he’s representing the board of education, not just himself.”

Ervin has since strongly defended himself, insisting the student had simply asked “good smart questions.”

“I mean, I was impressed and the other board members was impressed because she the question she asked,” he told WJHL.

“And, you know, I’m old school. I’m an old farm boy. And I didn’t mean nothing by anything. I just was proud of her.”



Ervin also claimed there was “a lot of context missing” from the now viral clip.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

An emergency meeting has been scheduled for Wednesday where the board is expected to censure him, while a protest has also been arranged.

Ervin – who is seeking re-election – can only be removed through a recall vote, which would require the support of two thirds of registered voters who cast ballots in the last election.

News.title: Iran reveals 10-point deal ‘agreed with Trump’…but $500bn ‘tollbooth’ in Strait of Hormuz & nuke enrichment could remain
News.content:
IRAN’S ten-point plan over ending the war in the Middle East has been revealed after the US agreed to a conditional two-week ceasefire.

Donald Trump called the proposed peace plan “workable” as he said Tehran prevented a “civilisation-ending blitz” but warned there is a lot of work still to be done.





Trump said the plan, which was brokered by Pakistan, was enough to facilitate a temporary truce between Washington and Tehran at the eleventh hour.

Peace talks over a permanent ceasefire are now set to get underway this week with both sides agreeing to listen to each other’s demands.

Details of Iran‘s ten-point deal have been released by Tehran’s state broadcaster and include several noteworthy additions and some major omissions.



A big part of the proposal is centred around the Strait of Hormuz which has become the focal point of the conflict across the last five weeks.

Iran closed off the vital waterway, which sees around 20 per cent of the world’s oil and natural gas pass through, when the conflict broke out.

The move essentially choked out global trade in the Gulf and drove the price of gas and oil through the roof across the world.

Tehran even threatened to attack any foreign vessel attempting to pass through as they laid down mines across the seabed.



Trump has made it one of his top goals of the war to reopen the Strait – a move which Iran has now agreed to.

The US president said on Truth Social that both sides have now agreed to America helping to open up the waterway immediately.

US warships will monitor the traffic along the Persian Gulf which has built up ever since Iran closed off the vital waterway, he added.

Iran's 10-point peace plan in full IRAN'S state broadcaster has revealed a ten-point plan which was reportedly sent to the US to help broker a long term peace deal. Complete cessation of the war on Iraq, Lebanon, and Yemen Complete and permanent cessation of the war on Iran with no time limit Ending all conflicts in the region in their entirety Reopening the Strait of Hormuz Establishing a protocol and conditions to ensure freedom and security of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz Full payment of compensation for reconstruction costs to Iran Full commitment to lifting sanctions on Iran Release of Iranian funds and frozen assets held by the United States Iran fully commits to not seeking possession of any nuclear weapons Immediate ceasefire takes effect on all fronts immediately upon approval of the above conditions

However, under Iran’s plan, they will remain in control of the Strait and be able to charge other nations to use it as they have been doing since the war started.

Iran is reportedly charging foreign vessels a toll of at least $1-a-barrel if they wish to pass through the 21-mile route.



Fees must reportedly be paid in Chinese currency or in crypto to the IRGC with the average cost for a single international oil tanker reaching $2million (£1.5m).

This “tollbooth” could see Iran make over $500billion (£372bn) if all ships are made to pay the hefty fee.

Iran has also agreed not to build nuclear weapons – the main reason why the US started the conflict over a month ago.

Washington believes the regime was just weeks away from developing a nuke capable of wiping out their enemies.



But questions have been raised over one of Iran’s proposals which differ in the Farsi and English versions shared among journalists.

In the Farsi-language plan, the mullahs included a term saying it would agree to the “acceptance of enrichment”.

This was not mentioned in any English copies – leading to fears the regime may try and remain able to enrich uranium, which is used to create nuclear weapons.



Speaking to Agence France-Presse after the deal was laid out, Trump said he isn’t worried that Iran could go back to rebuilding its nuclear stockpiles after the war.

He made it clear that the uranium will be “perfectly taken care of”.

Trump said the two-week ceasefire will help give Iran and the US time to finalise a proper deal which is likely to differ from Iran’s ten-point plan.

Two of the terms demand the complete cessation of the war on Iraq, Lebanon, and Yemen and the end of the war in Iran “with no time limit”.

Another mentions ending all conflicts in the Middle East after Iran retaliated by striking neighbours such as the UAE, Bahrain and Kuwait.



US forces have not launched any attacks on Iran since the ceasefire came into effect.

Yet the UAE and Israel have both they are continuing to detect missiles fired from Iran.

Israel is also part of the two-week ceasefire deal and has agreed to stop bombing while negotiations continue.



Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has warned that while he will accept the terms with Iran, Israel won’t wane in their war on Lebanon.

Israel has been fighting a two-pronged war in the Middle East in recent weeks against Iran but also its proxy in Hezbollah.

Netanyahu has vowed to eliminate the terror group from Lebanon in order to restore peace in the nation.

Three other terms laid out by Iran focus on the economy.

It includes compensation to help reconstruct Iran after the five-week bombing campaign, a full commitment to lifting sanctions on Iran and the release of Iranian funds and frozen assets held by the US.



Trump has since warned Washington won’t leave the Middle East completely due to the threat of Iran’s terror regime still existing.

He warned his military would he “hangin’ around” in order to make sure that peace is secured.

“This could be the Golden Age of the Middle East,” Trump added.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

UK Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer responded to the truce this morning by saying: “Together with our partners we must do all we can to support and sustain this ceasefire, turn it into a lasting agreement and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.”

Starmer is travelling to the Gulf today to meet leaders in the region to “discuss diplomatic efforts to support and uphold the ceasefire”.

News.title: Doctor strike ‘deliberately timed to cause havoc’, NHS boss says
News.content:
Doctor strike ‘deliberately timed to cause havoc’, NHS boss says

NHS England chief executive Sir Jim Mackey slams the British Medical Association as health leaders urge patients to still come forward for care

View 3 Images Sir Jim has spoken out about the timing of the doctors' strike (Image: PA)

The boss of the NHS says the doctors’ strike “has been deliberately timed to cause havoc”.

‌



It comes as NHS England is urging patients to still come forward to hospitals and GPs if they need care, amid fears some seriously unwell will delay getting help. Its chief executive Sir Jim Mackey told health leaders that hospitals were in "as good a place as we could hope" after the first day of the walkout.

‌



More recent strikes since Sir Jim took charge of the NHS have seen the health service manage to still carry out 95% of planned appointments, but this six-day walkout comes during the Easter school holidays when many staff will have booked annual leave.

‌



View 3 Images Sir Jim wrote to hospital bosses after the first day of the strike (Image: PA)

Sir Jim wrote a letter to hospital leaders on Tuesday evening which said: "I know today has been tough for staff picking up the strain across the country - and how disruptive and challenging it's been for many hospitals to manage it and fill their rotas following the Easter weekend.

"We cannot forget this action has been deliberately timed to cause havoc. There's a long way to go, but it looks like we're in as good a place as we could hope on day one.

‌



"I am so grateful to everyone for all you've done ahead of today, during today and what you will be doing over the next five plus days to contend with these pressures, maintain services and help keep the show on the road for our patients."

View 3 Images Doctors on a picket line outside the Royal Victoria Infirmary in Newcastle (Image: Andy Commins)

It comes after new YouGov polling found that 55% of British adults oppose resident doctors going on strike. Some 37% said they support the action, according to the survey of 4,385 adults in Britain.

‌



The six-day walkout which started at 7am on Tuesday is the 15th by resident doctors since 2023 and the joint-longest. It is the 60th day of strike action in the industrial dispute which started under the previous Conservative government. NHS estimates have put the cost at about £50 million a day for staff cover and rescheduled operations.

NHS England has urged patients to attend planned appointments unless they have been contacted to reschedule. It says GP practices, NHS 111 and urgent and emergency care services continue to be available. Hospital trusts are also working to protect priority treatments such as urgent surgery and cancer care.

Professor Ramani Moonesinghe, National Clinical Director for Critical and Perioperative Care at NHS England, said: “Staff across the NHS will be doing everything they can this week to keep patients safe and ensure people can continue to get the care they need.

‌



"We know this round of industrial action will be difficult, coming straight after the Easter weekend, but patients should come forward as normal and attend any appointments unless they are contacted otherwise. The NHS remains open for you this week – as ever, please call 999 or come to A&E in an emergency, and use 111 online first if you need urgent but not life-threatening help."

Resident doctors, those below the level of consultant, are on picket lines protesting against pay erosion which they want returning to 2008 levels. The BMA says real terms pay is down a fifth since then according to the retail price index (RPI). The doctors' union stresses that with RPI inflation running at 3.6%, their headline pay offer of 3.5% for 2026/27 is still a real-terms pay cut.

Health Secretary Wes Streeting has said the overall package of measures would have led to resident doctors getting an average pay rise of 4.9%. It also included reimbursement for exam costs and an additional 1,000 medical training places.

Article continues below

The BMA’s resident doctors committee (RDC) rejected the offer without putting it to a vote by members. It claims Mr Streeting’s team made a late change to the deal so that some of the pay rise would be phased in over three years.

RDC chair Dr Jack Fletcher said: "What the Health Secretary is asking us to reconsider now is essentially will you bake in more real terms pay cuts, not just this year, but for future years? So we're more than willing to reconsider, or meet the Health Secretary and reconsider any offer that he puts to us. However, we can't accept further real terms pay cuts."

Most other NHS staff including nurses and midwives have only been offered 3.3% for 2026-27. Other public sector staff including 1.5 million council workers have been awarded a 3.3 per cent pay rise.

News.title: BBC Morning Live Dr Xand gives 'hottest' clothes tip to keep Norovirus away
News.content:
BBC Morning Live Dr Xand gives 'hottest' clothes tip to keep Norovirus away

BBC Morning Live Dr Xand van Tulleken says a little thought can kill infections in your home - and save you cash

View 2 Images BBC Morning Live's Dr Xand said it can boost your household's health (Image: BBC Morning Live)

The ongoing Middle East conflict has caused energy prices to soar. Despite a ceasefire being agreed, gas and electricity bills are still widely expected to climb once the current price cap expires.

‌



As a result, households need to be more vigilant than ever regarding their energy consumption. One medical expert is urging people to pay close attention to the temperature at which they're washing their clothes.

‌



However, the concerns extend beyond simply saving money. Appearing on BBC's Morning Live, Dr Xand van Tulleken warned that your washing machine temperature can also carry significant implications for your health.

‌



He explained: "Hottest your washing machine will go is 90 degrees usually, and that will kill everything. It's almost boiling it, it's bad for the clothes, it's very expensive. Whatever's happened to those clothes, I think you've got to get new clothes at that point.

"Sixty degrees, certain bugs will be killed and that can be quite good. So if you've got an infection going around your house, particularly think of something like norovirus, put it up at 60. Along with the mechanical cleaning and the detergent, that's quite good.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



"Personally, I don't see the point in 40 degrees, because it's too hot to be cheap and it's too cold to kill anything. Commit to one of the other; either go hot or go cold.

"Thirty degrees, that gets the job done, it is much cheaper. So going from 40 to 30 saves you almost 40% in energy costs. It's quicker; make sure you get a lower temperature detergent.

"And then 20 degrees; I've got to say I'm a 20 degrees guy for everything except my workout clothes, which go in hotter. 20 degrees saves 62% of your money compared to 40, so that is a big deal."

‌



What temperature works best for washing machines?

According to consumer group Which?, many of us typically run the washing machine at 40C, though 60C remains the most frequently used setting. The organisation backs Dr Xand's view that 60C effectively eliminates germs: "Ideally, you need to be washing items at 60C with a good quality detergent to effectively remove germs and other nasties.

"Think of 60C as a hot wash. Washing at 60C generally cleans slightly better than the 40°C program, especially on greasy stains. However, running costs increase by more than half.

"Washing at 40C should do the job for most stains, but serious soiling might need a blast at 60°C. Yes, you can wash clothes at 20°C - it's an excellent energy-saving option. It's best for lightly soiled clothing though. Heavily stained items usually benefit from being washed at a higher temperature."

‌



But what about 90C? Which? experts explain: "Think of 90°C as a very hot wash. It's the hottest wash program you'll find on most machines and is only suitable for a few items, as many labels won't recommend washing at such a high temperature.

"The NHS website states that you should wash underwear, towels and household linen at 60°C to prevent the spread of germs, or at 40°C with a bleach-based laundry product (we suggest bio washing powder). It says nothing about washing at as high as 90°C to kill bacteria.

"And while washing at such a high temperature should certainly help to banish stains, only use it when the fabric is robust enough to stand up to the heat. Always check the label."

‌



View 2 Images Dr Xand urged people to speak to their GP rather than turning to the drugs being illegally sold (Image: BBC)

So are cooler washes the way forward? Not quite. Dr Xand pointed out that while lower temperatures could be kinder on your energy bills, they bring their own set of problems.

He went on to say: "But at the lower temperatures, you've got to think about cleaning your machine. One is that the tray that you put out-the detergent tray where all the mould grows-that can be a real nuisance to clean. I put it in the dishwasher.

Article continues below

"And then mechanical cleaning of the drum. Just a cloth, some vinegar - wiping is really good. And if your machine has a cleaning cycle which runs at a high temperature, do that according to the manufacturer's instructions. And then air it out."

News.title: Israeli intelligence FURIOUS over Trump ceasefire and determined to continue Iran war
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Israeli intelligence FURIOUS over Trump ceasefire and determined to continue Iran war

US President Donald Trump has pulled back at the last minute from imposing further hell on Iranian regime as the Strait of Hormuz is freed up for two weeks - but Israel keeps up attacks

View 5 Images This is what ceasefire looks like in Lebanon this morning (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Israeli intelligence is ‘furious’ over the so-called Trump-Iran ceasefire deal and is likely to do all it can to undermine it and continue the war, sources have told the Mirror. A western security source says the Israeli Mossad agency and Military Intelligence does not believe it has achieved all of its aims in the war, despite Trump’s claims of a major success.

‌



The nuclear enrichment pile still remains buried in Tehran’s nuke facilities, it still has half of its missile capability and thousands of deadly drones remain in its underground tunnel facilities. Our source told the Mirror: “The Israeli intelligence community is deeply unhappy about this so-called deal as it has not achieved anywhere near what it wanted to in this conflict. They believe it is way too early and Iran has retained some of its capability in terms of missiles and drones so it remains a threat to Israeli cities and its citizens. It is highly likely that Israel will try to undermine what Trump claims he has achieved because this was Israel’s once chance at smashing the Iranian threat. It’s not there yet.”

‌



View 5 Images Warthog US warplaneabove RAF Lakenheath, UK (Image: Getty Images)

‌



OPINION Christopher Bucktin Why Trump's chilling Iran threats should still make us all fear despite ceasefire

Trump agreed to a two-week ceasefire with Iran, less than two hours before his deadline for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face devastating attacks. It was a seismic turnaround from earlier in the day, when he said “a whole civilisation will die tonight” if his demands were not met.

Pakistan’s military chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, and its prime minister, Shehbaz Sharif, helped mediate the ceasefire. Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said Tehran would cease counter-attacks and provide safe passage through the waterway, if attacks against it stop.

‌



View 5 Images 'Hollow celebration' US President Donald Trump (Image: LENIN NOLLY/SIPA/Shutterstock)

Trump said on social media: “This will be a double sided ceasefire. The reason for doing so is that we have already met and exceeded all Military objectives, and are very far along with a definitive agreement concerning long-term peace with Iran, and peace in the Middle East.” A temporary halt in fighting and the reopening of Hormuz would allow Middle Eastern exporters to ship significant volumes of oil that have been trapped inside the Gulf since hostilities began.

Trump told reporters it was a “total and complete victory”. The war, now in its sixth week, has claimed more than 5,000 lives in nearly a dozen countries, including more than 1,600 civilians in Iran. Publicly Israel supported the decision to suspend strikes on Iran for the two-week period, Prime Minister Binyamin Netanyahu’s office said.

‌



View 5 Images Iranians burn US and Israeli flags during a demonstration following the ceasefire announcement (Image: ABEDIN TAHERKENAREH/EPA/Shutterstock)

But crucially the ceasefire does not apply to Lebanon, it added, in an apparent contradiction to comments from Pakistan’s Sharif who said it included a cessation of Israel’s Lebanon campaign. Further shaking faith in Trump’s claims, after his announcement, the Israeli military said it had identified missiles launched from Iran, and explosions from intercepted missiles were heard in Tel Aviv.

Gulf countries including Kuwait, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates also issued near-simultaneous alerts and activated air defences. Israeli media said its military was striking back at launch sites in Iran.

‌



But within Israel and elsewhere it is believed Trump has ‘kicked the can down the road’ in the hope that the US can try to talk Iran down from its ten point plan for long-term peace. And whilst the Strait of Hormuz may have been opened - giving the international oil trade a temporary reprieve - Iran retains control of it at a price.

Israel has underlined a lack of faith in the peace deal this morning by launching major attacks across southern Lebanon and slapping evacuation orders on Lebanese citizens. The ten point Iranian-imposed peace demands that Trump claims as a ‘complete victory’ appear near-impossible to accept for Israel or American in its entirety.

View 5 Images Women carry portrait of Iran's slain supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei as they celebrate ceasefire in Srinagar (Image: Basit Zargar/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Article continues below

Iran will also likely demand a $2 million price for every ship to pass through thr Strait of Hormuz. It includes the lifting of all primary and secondary sanctions on Iran. Iran demands continued Iranian control over the strait of Hormuz, US military withdrawal from the Middle East, an end to attacks on Iran and its allies and the release of frozen Iranian assets. Tehran also insists it wants a UN security council resolution making any deal binding, thereby making it illegal for anyone to break the deal.

Crucially the plan is believed to demand ‘acceptance of enrichment,’ and it is believed to demand ‘reparations’ for damage imposed on Iran during the war. Sources say much of the plan is ‘unworkable’ for the US, such as the complete withdrawal of the US military from the Middle East. And tensions between Iran and Israel have not been resolved, with attacks on Iran’s proxy forces such as Hezbollah and even Iran itself continuing.

News.title: Man orders groceries for delivery but is left fuming at cheeky word on bag
News.content:
Man orders groceries for delivery but is left fuming at cheeky word on bag

A man placed an online order for food and other essential items to be delivered to his doorstep but when it arrived, he saw one word had been repeatedly written all over his bags

View Image The man spotted one word written over and over again on his food delivery bags (stock image) (Image: Getty Images)

A man ordered a food shop online but when it was delivered, he spotted one word written repeatedly all over his reusable bags.

‌



Online deliveries can be a serious help for busy working people, those with mobility struggles, transport issues and more. Typically, customers add all the items they wish to purchase to an online trolley and select an appropriate delivery time. Delivery drivers then drop off the selected products at their door.

‌



But one American man, who posted on Reddit using the handle @felipe_the_dog, was baffled after spotting his delivery bags from his Whole Foods order had the word “tips” written all over them.

‌



He assumed the delivery driver had done this and said: “I don’t normally do grocery delivery at all, but my wife wanted two items that aren’t carried in our local stores so I made a small $35 order. I didn’t even see a tip option when placing the order.

“After seeing the bags this morning, I investigated and saw a $5 tip applied automatically to the order. I’m okay with that. Then I read that the drivers can’t even see who tips, so is this person writing this on every bag on their route? That’s insane and I feel like would get them fired.”

Here in Britain, tipping a delivery driver isn’t all that common - especially if they work for a large supermarket chain where delivery services incur a small fee. For companies where delivery workers are self-employed or classed as independent contractors, many people do provide tips.

‌



In the UK, tipping is appreciated though not often expected. Minimum wage is enforced and businesses have to pay their staff the full amount, meaning customers aren’t pressured into subsidising staff members’ wages like they are in America.

Tipping is a hallmark of American culture but in many online forums, people are sharing their frustration with the increasing pressure to tip, even in businesses where it wouldn’t typically be expected. This appears to be the case with Felipe’s groceries order.

‌



In the comments section, fellow Reddit users shared their thoughts. One person said: “Make a review with those pictures. On yelp, on their website etc. That’s unprofessional and distasteful."

Another agreed: “Definitely file a complaint. I reuse my bags, but I’d toss these immediately. What a waste.”

A third said: “That’s pathetic. Report that through Amazon, I suspect you should be receiving an invite for feedback after delivery.”

‌



Someone else said: “Weird that you're okay with the equivalent of someone reaching into your wallet and taking $5 without saying anything and only noticing because it's missing.”

Another said: “You shouldn’t be okay with them charging you what you didn’t authorise."

One person commented: “Tips should be opt in and not opt out. They auto add a tip that you have to notice and then cancel. Should be the opposite if you want to add a tip.”

‌



And another shared: “I don’t order from grocery services that ask for tips. I know I’m in a fortunate position to be able to pick up, I’m very close to all the stores and also have a car.

“We can’t keep allowing tipping in additional industries. It’s already entrenched in food service, fine. But why is it starting to be everywhere now.”

Some people suggested management, and not the delivery driver, were behind the handwritten “tips” message all over the bag so drivers knew which customers had tipped before they proceeded with the delivery.

Article continues below

But Felipe added: “Like I said I don’t mind the $5 default tip for the driver. I just don’t like s*** written on my bags. If none of the bags were marked, wouldn’t the drivers have to treat them all equally?”

News.title: Sarah Ferguson 'turns to ex lovers for support' as she 'stays away from Andrew'
News.content:
Sarah Ferguson 'turns to ex lovers for support' as she 'stays away from Andrew'

Fergie has gone to ground in the wake of the Epstein scandal - but sources claim she has turned to two of her former flames to help keep her location under wraps

View 3 Images Sarah Ferguson is being supported by some discreet and wealthy friends, according to reports (Image: the_anti_slavery_collective/Instagram)

Where in the world is Sarah Ferguson? It's been months now since the disgraced former duchess was last seen in public, with whispers swirling that she's been in destinations as far flying as Dubai, Switzerland and Ireland. But her exact location remains a mystery.

Fergie, 66, is said to be on a 'secret sofa-surfing world tour' which has seen her moving from the home of one loyal and discreet friend to another. She is also reportedly in possession of three different mobile phones as she continues to hide out.

One pal, describing Andrew's ex-wife as 'dishevelled', said this week that Sarah "really is low". They added that she hasn't been taking care of her roots or keeping up with her Botox, and continually rotates through her three phones because she is afraid of being tracked.

View 3 Images Sarah with her then-boyfriend Count Gaddo della Gherardesca (Image: Press Association)

A source told the Daily Mail: "She has been asking, 'How am I going to get through this?' She complains a lot about being broke – although I don't know if that is broke in the sense that you or I would understand it. Her friends have been joking that they wouldn't be surprised to find her selling her old handbags on Vinted."

Sarah is said to be on speaking terms with her ex-husband Andrew Mountbatten Windsor - but the bond that once saw her declare them to be the 'happiest divorced couple in the world' has been broken. As she distances herself from Andrew, Fergie is believed to have turned to some of her former flames in order to keep her location under wraps.

Article continues below

According to the friend, the ex-royal is currently staying somewhere that is like a castle and has an Italian count looking after her. And the count in question could be Count Gaddo della Gherardesca, her boyfriend between late 1997 and early 1998 following her divorce from Andrew. The 86-year-old has an enormous home in Tuscany, as well as a ski lodge in Verbier.

View 3 Images Paddy McNally is also said to have come to Fergie's aid (Image: ExpressStar)

It's not the only ex alleged to have come to Sarah's aid. Last month it was reported that she was hiding at the Wiltshire home of 88-year-old Paddy McNally. She dated the former racing driver and motorsports executive for three years before marrying Andrew, and the pair have remained close. He also has properties in the Swiss ski resort Verbier and in St Tropez in the south of France.

Article continues below

Sarah seems to be reliant on the kindness of her loyal, wealthy friends. According to the one source, there are a number of people - including some well-known names - that are still quietly faithful to Fergie and wealthy enough to house her. But they want to keep that connection under wraps.

It comes after reports that Sarah feels "incredibly betrayed" by members of the Royal Family in the wake of the Epstein scandal. A source told Heat World the mother of two is "very bitter" following the fallout, adding: "What people don't see is just how low she's sunk. Every time she opens a paper or goes online, it's another reminder that she's completely on the outside and there's no real way back, and she's really struggling to come to terms with that.

"Instead of dealing with it, she's numbing it — and that's only making everything worse. It fuels a cycle where she starts ranting and then feels even more isolated the next day."

News.title: Fuel stations where petrol and diesel cost drops 'will be passed on quickly'
News.content:
Fuel stations where petrol and diesel cost drops 'will be passed on quickly'

Developments in the Middle East conflict have sparked hope that prices are about to top out after weeks of rapid rises

View 2 Images UK motorists have been hit hard (Image: Getty Images)

Since conflict between the USA, Israel and Iran sparked an economic bombshell through March, petrol and diesel prices in the UK have risen sharply. Drivers had been enjoying stable and reasonably affordable costs over the first two months of 2026, before that came to an abrupt halt.

‌



In the weeks since strikes were first launched at the end of February, petrol drivers have seen prices rise by around 25p per litre, while diesel drivers have been hit even harder - having no choice but to stomaches of around 50p in that time.

‌



However, news of a two-week ceasefire overnight and fresh moves to reopen the vital oil shipping lane of the Strait of Hormuz has seen oil prices drop substantially, albeit they remain well above where they were before the conflict began. It has sparked cautious hope that pump prices may start to fall.

‌



RAC head of policy Simon Williams said: “The average price of a litre of unleaded is now at 157.71p - up 25p (19%) since the war began - while diesel has exceeded the 190p mark (190.62p) and is up 48p (34%) since February 28.

"Both fuels are now at their most expensive since late 2022.

"The conditional ceasefire announcement may have taken some heat out of global oil prices, but the outlook for drivers in the UK remains highly uncertain.

‌



"The best hope in the short term is that pump prices stop rising at the rate they have been and hopefully top out in the coming days.

View 2 Images Fuel prices have rocketed (Image: OLI SCARFF, AFP via Getty Images)

"Much will depend on the stability of the ceasefire, whether oil shipments can move freely through the Strait of Hormuz, and the longer‑term impact on oil production across the Gulf.

Article continues below

"As it is a sustained lower oil price - over several weeks, not just a few days - that is required to bring wholesale fuel costs down meaningfully.

"Drivers should not expect significantly cheaper fuel in the short term, although some smaller independent forecourts buying on a 'spot’ basis may be quicker to pass on any reductions.

“We continue to recommend drivers shop around for fuel and make use of free apps like myRAC to ensure they always get the best price each time they fill up."

News.title: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor FINALLY moves into new home after Prince Edward clash
News.content:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor FINALLY moves into new home after Prince Edward clash

The King's brother has finally moved into Marsh Farm in Norfolk following a 'quiet word' from Prince Edward about his temporary accommodation at nearby Wood Farm

View 4 Images Andrew's younger brother Edward spoke to him about his living arrangements (Image: PA)

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has at last settled into his new Norfolk residence following his recent Easter confrontation with Prince Edward regarding his interim living arrangements, according to reports.

‌



The disgraced former Duke of York was allegedly approached by his brother, the Duke of Edinburgh, for a "quiet word" about relocating to his permanent home in exile shortly before the Easter break. Andrew was relocated to Norfolk in February after troubling revelations about his association with convicted paedophile Jeffrey Epstein surfaced in the most recent batch of documents released by the US. He's always denied any wrongdoing.

‌



He was staying temporarily at Wood Farm while refurbishment work at the neighbouring Marsh Farm was being completed.

‌



View 4 Images Marsh Farm is within the Sandringham Estate (Image: Getty)

Inside Prince Edward's Easter Garden House getaway after Andrew forces duke into holiday READ MORE :

However, the disgraced royal seemed to be "dragging his heels" about moving into his permanent new residence and had a meeting with Edward, who was supposed to stay at Wood Farm last week but was unable to because his brother remained there.

It was claimed that Prince Edward and wife Sophie had to use a 'holiday let' instead of their original plans. The couple ended up using Garden House for their Easter break, which can cost £4,110 a week to rent out in peak season. A source said: "Andrew was evicted from Royal Lodge at Windsor but now has two homes at his disposal. He is just going back and forth between Wood Farm and Marsh Farm. It’s got to be sorted as Edward and Sophie like to use Wood Farm."

‌



Fresh reports now claim that the disgraced royal has finally transferred to Marsh Farm and spent his first night there on Easter Monday. He was photographed walking between the two properties with his dogs, reports the Express. According to the Daily Mail, Andrew's staff were also spotted arriving at the farm, transporting bags into the building.

View 4 Images Marsh Farm has undergone renovations including the addition of a Sky dish (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Wood Farm and Marsh Farm both sit on the Sandringham estate in Norfolk, around two miles from King Charles' main Sandringham House. Andrew's new home at Marsh Farm is far smaller than his grand Royal Lodge at Windsor Castle, as the disgraced ex-prince is set to downgrade from the 30-bedroom property to the Marsh Farm property which has five bedrooms and two bathrooms.

Marsh Farm sits next to a country road, surrounded by farmland and open countryside, and while it is smaller than Royal Lodge it does boast outbuildings and stables. It is situated in the same village as Wood Farm, where he was staying while renovation work was carried out. Renovations included luxury carpets, a Sky dish, a fast broadband connection and a security fence.

Wolferton has a church, some small businesses and a social club, but f or Andrew, the closest Co-Op and Chinese takeaway are 3.2 miles away in the village of Dersingham. Wood Farm was where Andrew's father, Prince Philip, the late Duke of Edinburgh, spent much of his retirement. The late Queen said that her husband "loved" the property, partly because the "sea was so close".

‌



View 4 Images Entrance to Wood Farm on the Sandringham Estate (Image: PA)

Originally a large farmhouse, Wood Farm was converted into two cottages over the years and used as a regular informal weekend retreat for the royals - particualrly when it came to annual shooting parties. Andrew's ex-wife Sarah Ferguson stayed there alone multiple times as a guest of the late Queen following her separation from Andrew in the 90s.

Article continues below

Teresa Thompson, the cottage's retired housekeeper, said in 2022: "All the Royal Family love Wood Farm, because it's out of the way, it's small, it's intimate. You haven't got lots of officials and household, it's just the close staff. And they literally can relax in the family house, it's wonderful, and I had a wonderful 22 years down there, it was the best time of my life without a doubt."

This follows closely after the King's brother was confronted by demonstrators at his new Norfolk home, in what's been characterised as a significant security lapse. On Maundy Thursday, a group of demonstrators allegedly scaled the fence at Marsh Farm before being challenged by security personnel.

In photographs captured by Bav Media, several individuals were spotted having gained access near the farmhouse, where Andrew had been seen driving to earlier, and began "shouting abuse". They were quickly intercepted by Andrew's security team.

News.title: Temperatures in UK to peak at 26C on Wednesday
News.content:
All four nations of the UK recorded their highest temperature of the year so far on Tuesday after very warm air was dragged in from continental Europe.

The addition of the foehn effect - a warming wind on the leeside of a mountain - meant that north-west Wales saw the highest temperatures.

Wales - 24.8C (76.7F) - Mona, Isle of Anglesey

England - 22.5C (72.5F) - Merryfield, Somerset

Scotland - 22.5C (72.5F) - Kinloss, Moray

Northern Ireland - 19.0C (66.2F) - Armagh, County Armagh

Most of England and Wales will be dry and sunny again on Wednesday with a gentle south to south-easterly breeze.

Some cloud will move into parts of northern England and Wales, especially in the afternoon, and it won't be as warm along western coasts.

The focus of the highest temperatures on Wednesday will be the Midlands, East Anglia and south-east England, possibly reaching 26C (79F) in some localised spots.

This is around 10C above average for early April.

The last time before this week that 25C or more was recorded in the UK was 19 September 2025, when temperatures peaked at 27.8C at St James's Park, London.

Around this time in April in 2017 and 2020 25C (77F) was recorded, but last year that temperature was not reached until the last day of the month.

The highest temperature ever recorded in the UK in April was 29.4C (84.9F) measured in London in 1949.

There is some way to go to beat that but spring is the fastest warming season due to climate change.

Scotland and Northern Ireland will not be as warm. The cloud will break to give some sunshine and temperatures could still reach as high as 18C (64F) in eastern Scotland.

News.title: I’ve never shopped at FatFace, but its spring drop has impressed me
News.content:
The arrival of spring might have you craving a seasonal wardrobe refresh: puffer coats and boots are out, while floaty dresses and linen separates are in. But forget George at Asda or Next, it’s FatFace that’s the surprising label on my radar for 2026.

Catering for all your sunny weather needs, the British brand has undergone a stylish revamp in recent years. What began in the late 80s as an adventure label selling branded jumpers and T-shirts out the back of a camper van, has evolved into one of the most recognisable brands on the UK high street.

Originally known for its outdoor gear, FatFace is named after the "La Face" ski slope in Val d'Isère. Circa 2010, it was associated with frumpy fashion – but it’s now a favourite among women seeking practical yet stylish everyday clothing, parents looking for well-crafted kidswear and men looking for a elevated staples.

I’ll admit, I’ve always been more likely to shop at Zara, Cos and & Other Stories – but FatFace’s new drop for spring has impressed me. Think wide leg linen trousers, wedding guest-appropriate dresses and hero denim pieces.

Despite its new fashion-forward approach, the quality of the clothing remains – as do the accessible prices. If you’re shopping for a spring capsule wardrobe, FatFace is well worth a browse. Here’s everything I’ve added to my basket, from dresses to bags.

open image in gallery ( Fat Face )

Every spring and summer wardrobe can benefit from a pair of white linen wide leg trousers. This FatFace pair nail the brief. The loose, laidback cut is paired with a mid-rise waist and pockets for extra practicality.

open image in gallery ( Fat Face )

This chocolate brown dress is perfect for throwing on when you don’t know what to wear – but the neutral shade means you can style it into autumn, too. Characterised by its flattering square neckline and long, puffed sleeves, the maxi length and cinched-in waist are universally flattering.

open image in gallery ( Fat Face )

Don’t sleep on FatFace for occasion wear. This timeless dress features a bandeau neckline, fitted body and A-line midi skirt. Polka dot is everywhere this season and its brown colourway makes it easy to dress up or down.

open image in gallery ( Fat Face )

As we ease into summer, these longline denim shorts will become your most-worn piece. Designed with a flattering high waist and vintage faded wash, the Bermuda-style shorts are cut just above the knee. Style them with ballet flats day to day before swapping to kitten heels in the evening.

open image in gallery ( Fat Face )

This midi skirt is endlessly wearable. Complete with a comfortable elasticated waistband, the skirt features a button down front and monochrome polka dot print. Adding intrigue to an everyday white T-shirt, the skirt also comes with a matching top.

open image in gallery ( FatFace )

You’d never guess this chocolate brown suede bag hailed from the high street. The buckle detailing nods to DeMellier while the capacious size makes it perfect for a work bag.

I tried on M&S’s new spring collection – here’s what to shop (and what to avoid)

News.title: Trump just TACO’d away American credibility as he backs down on Iran threats
News.content:

Donald Trump has spent his career railing against elite presidents who did not have the courage to act the way he claims he does.

But judging by Trump’s announcement today that he would extend the deadline for his strikes within Iran by two weeks, one has to wonder what the president’s words mean any more. He makes big threats, but quickly becomes the boy who cries wolf and doesn’t follow through. While nobody wanted to see him end a “civilization”, his latest retreat is just more evidence that his big threats mean little and will now carry political consequences.

Trump’s decision to back out – commonly referred to as “TACO” or “Trump always chickens out” – this time demonstrates a measure of strategic weakness that far outmeasures any previous humiliation that Trump used to criticize from past presidents.

And it means that no world leader ever needs to take Trump’s threats seriously.

open image in gallery Donald Trump has backed off his latest Iran threats, bringing back the ‘Trump always chickens out’ nickname ( Getty Images )

Trump knows what happens when presidents make empty threats because he criticized them for it. In 2013, Trump lambasted Barack Obama for walking back from his self-imposed “red line” that if then-Syrian President Bashar al-Assad would use chemical weapons, the United States would respond.

“The only reason President Obama wants to attack Syria is to save face over his very dumb RED LINE statement. Do NOT attack Syria, fix U.S.A.” Trump said at the time.

But if Obama refused to impose his artificial red line, Trump did his best matador impression and waved a gigantic red banner in front of the bull that is Iran. He did so over the weekend when he declared Tuesday “Power Plant Day” and “Bridge Day” for U.S. armed forces unless Iran would “Open the F***in’ Strait, you crazy b*****ds,” lest they be “living in Hell”.

Trump escalated his threats when he said: “A whole civilization will die tonight, never to be brought back again.” There is no other way to describe what Trump threatened: war crimes and genocide. Trump brought the world to the brink of disaster and with Congress out of town, had nobody to rein him in, although the Republican-controlled House and Senate refused to do so.

Then, he backed off.

open image in gallery Trump began his attacks against Iran in late February and has continued to bomb the nation ( AFP via Getty Images )

Maybe Trump heard pleas from Pakistan’s prime minister Shehbaz Sharif to extend the deadline for two weeks. Perhaps he got the yips about the idea of engaging in a scorched-earth campaign against another country that would inevitably cost thousands of American lives, thereby turning him into another cog in the war machine against which he railed.

Maybe a phone call from House Speaker Mike Johnson said such a move would cost him the majority in the House and a text from Senate Majority Leader John Thune warned the Senate would go to the Democrats.

Whatever the rationale, Trump backed off the ledge.

But the world cannot breathe easily after this. Opening the option to attack civilian infrastructure cannot be undone. Now, the world will live in constant fear that Trump will carry through with his threats.

This opens the door for any malign actor to escalate. This is not a hypothetical: just months after Obama backed off his red line, Russian President Vladimir Putin invaded Crimea. Putin, to say nothing of China’s Xi Jinping, will look at Trump as weak and find license to do whatever they want, to borrow a Trumpism.

The opposite is also true. Now, every country will see Trump as the Sword of Damocles swinging its way across the globe. Again, this does not require imagination: Canada took Trump’s repeated threats to annex it seriously and adopted a more confrontational posture. The rest of the world have to adjust accordingly to a world where the United States can be hostile to international values.

open image in gallery Tehran can continue recovery operations after Trump agreed to a two-week ceasefire with Iran ( AFP via Getty Images )

In addition, Trump seems to have forgotten an adage from his first Defense Secretary James Mattis: the enemy gets a vote. Even if Trump backed down, Iran cannot be seen as taking these threats lying down. It will respond in kind either toward Arab allies of the United States or Israel. Iran will do so to make such a threat as painful as possible and warn the U.S. or other nations not to do so again.

So while, yes, Trump ultimately did not unleash the fury and cause incalculable loss of life, he has forever shifted how the United States relates to the rest of the world, and initiated a new phase of the Iran war.

A common refrain when Trump ran for president in 2016 was to take him seriously, not literally. However, today the world can’t afford to decipher when he is bluffing – which he is most of the time.

News.title: The Drama has a Zendaya problem
News.content:

The first rule of The Drama is: you do not talk about The Drama. This is the approach, at least, taken by the film’s marketing team, who have nurtured a near-total omertà when it comes to its much-vaunted Big Twist. Those who have seen The Drama – a terse and urticating comedy about nuclear-grade wedding jitters – will know this isn’t really a twist at all, but rather the core premise. It is revealed near the beginning, when bride-to-be Emma (Zendaya) drunkenly spills her most shameful secret to fiancé Charlie (Robert Pattinson). As a result, it’s impossible to talk about the film – or about Zendaya’s character – without flouting this particular spoiler. So let’s flout.

The secret Emma divulges is dark. Mariana-Trench dark. She explains that when she was 15 years old, she planned to commit a school shooting, going as far as to bring her father’s rifle into her high school before an abrupt change of heart. Charlie and his friends are scandalised. (Audiences too have been scandalised: in the build-up to its release, The Drama faced vocal criticism from anti-gun activists.) The twist, devised by writer-director Kristoffer Borgli, is reasonably effective as a dramatic catalyst, and, perversely, as a comic one. Pattinson’s character, destabilised by the realisation that he may be about to marry a would-be terrorist, spends much of the film neurotically spiralling, with increasingly wild results. At this wedding, the honeymoon period is over before the vows.

Now, The Drama is not really a film about school shootings. But the subject’s invocation was always going to dominate the conversation – particularly when it’s presented as it is, in narrative-bombshell form. There becomes, inevitably, an onus on the film to deliver not just seriocomic entertainment but meaningful social commentary. That it fails to do this falls squarely on Zendaya’s character.

Emma, you see, is an enigma. Charlie cannot read her, and neither can we – this is very much the point. The details of her flirtation with mass violence are confounding and opaque: the bullying that supposedly drove her towards it seems relatively banal (name-calling, jostling, but not the sort of psychological torment that is so often unearthed in real-life school-shooting cases). Moreover, her decision to abandon the planned attack and adopt a position of anti-gun advocacy is motivated less by any evident contrition and more by random whim.

open image in gallery Something new: Zendaya in ‘The Drama’ ( A24 )

By the present day, has she changed? Is she a meaningfully different person to her gun-loving teen self? These are the questions that ought to form the crux of Charlie’s moral dilemma, but Emma gives us nothing by way of answers. So they just hang there. Zendaya’s character hardly seems riddled with remorse or complex lingering pathologies. Perhaps this is in itself a satirical point – the idea that America has become so inured to gun violence that even school shootings are now part of the prosaic and unstimulating everyday, requiring no extraordinary evil or fanaticism. But on a narrative level, it creates a void. Zendaya isn’t playing a character; she’s playing a thought experiment.

None of the characters in The Drama are particularly multi-dimensional, but most are easy to parse – skeletal personalities blobbed with enough backstory to make them appear vaguely human-shaped. There’s a logic to them, even in their contradictions. We know that Charlie is dishonest, when it serves him – he lies about reading a book to land a first date with Emma – but that he has enough shame to later admit the truth. We know that Rachel (Alana Haim) has a mean, irresponsible streak, but a staunch disgust when it comes to Emma’s school-shooting fantasy. One of The Drama’s best-executed scenes sees Charlie interact with his colleague Misha (Hailey Benton Gates); over the course of one conversation, we glean her ambient self-hatred, which then quickly manifests in messy sexual acquiescence. All these characters are more intelligible, more real, than Emma is ever allowed to be.

open image in gallery Something blue: Zendaya in ‘The Drama’ ( A24 )

This sort of stubborn wooliness does not serve Zendaya’s strengths as an actor, either. The 29-year-old can be a terrific presence with the right material (Challengers and Dune: Part Two, for eg), and she’s one of the only young actors around who seems to have legitimate box office clout. (That The Drama made back its budget within the first week testifies to that.) Hell, she was even undeniable in Marvel’s Spider-Mans, as the laconic, thoroughly modern MJ. There, it was a case of doing a lot with a little – in The Drama, she’s given a lot and instructed to do nothing with it.

In this way, it’s easy to agree with the film’s detractors. By stripping away the psychological realities of mass violence, The Drama ends up unavoidably diluting it. Is this gross insensitivity or fair artistic licence? That’s up to interpretation. But then, in The Drama, so is everything else.

'The Drama' is in cinemas

News.title: All we know about Iran’s 10 point peace plan after agreeing two week ceasefire with US
News.content:
